headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection and data-leakage via LightAgent’s broad network/MCP/browser surfaces; Whisper is local-only and read-limited, reducing direct conflict but not eliminating unsafe handoff paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent can use MCP, browsers, and broad network egress, so it may ingest untrusted content and pass it onward. Whisper has no MCP, browser, or filesystem write surface, so it is not a direct injector, but if LightAgent forwards its outputs into Whisper workflows, prompt-like content could still be misinterpreted. The pathway exists, but not by default from Whisper alone.
conditions: IF LightAgent ingests web or MCP content and forwards it into downstream text-processing prompts
IF an operator manually copies LightAgent output into a Whisper-adjacent workflow
mitigations: Restrict LightAgent to trusted MCP servers only
Disable browser-driven ingestion for untrusted pages
Insert a human review step before forwarding outputs
Use provenance tags on all LightAgent-generated text
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent touches user conversations, long-term memory, tool results, and provenance metadata, and it has broad network egress. Whisper is local-only with no network egress and only audio-file inputs, so it is less likely to exfiltrate directly. The pair still creates a leakage path if sensitive LightAgent state is routed into Whisper inputs or if LightAgent sends those data classes to third parties.
conditions: IF LightAgent forwards conversations, memory, or tool results to external APIs
IF audio files fed to Whisper contain sensitive content derived from LightAgent state
mitigations: Limit LightAgent egress to approved endpoints
Avoid passing sensitive text into audio conversion pipelines
Redact secrets before any cross-agent transfer
Log and review outbound requests from LightAgent
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filtering at the orchestrator

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightAgent supports multiple instances and can spawn subprocesses, while Whisper cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or use MCP. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The main overlap is read/processing of user-provided content, so contention is limited unless an external orchestrator gives Whisper additional mutable access not shown in the profiles.
conditions: IF an external wrapper grants Whisper write access not present in its profile
IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable workspace by an orchestrator
mitigations: Keep Whisper in read-only mode
Separate working directories per agent
Avoid shared git worktrees
Serialize any shared preprocessing steps
requires-engineering: add lock coordination in the orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can produce tool results and workflow state that downstream systems may treat as authoritative. Whisper is a transformer model with command-line usage and no built-in verification layer, so if its outputs are chained into LightAgent or vice versa, errors can propagate without checks. The pair is not inherently dangerous, but the default handoff path can amplify mistakes.
conditions: IF LightAgent consumes Whisper transcripts as authoritative text
IF Whisper outputs are used to trigger LightAgent tool calls without validation
mitigations: Require explicit confidence thresholds before acting on outputs
Add a verification step between agents
Display source provenance alongside transcripts
Sample-check a subset of handoffs manually
requires-engineering: implement structured-output validation

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent handles user conversations, long-term memory, and tool results, which can create retention and residency obligations. Whisper touches only audio and speech and has no network egress or OAuth scopes, so the compliance mismatch is narrower than for a cloud pair. The main risk is policy mismatch on stored transcripts or audio artifacts, not a direct residency breach from Whisper itself.
conditions: IF audio or transcript artifacts are retained under different policies than LightAgent memory
IF regulated content is routed from LightAgent into Whisper processing
mitigations: Align retention settings for transcripts and memory
Delete temporary audio artifacts after processing
Document which data classes each agent may store
Review whether secrets are ever embedded in audio or transcripts
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data
